Each hour is the hour ending then, with the sun of half an hour earlier (15:00 = the sun at 14:30), for sun and heat alike. The **shadiest** walk minimises the shade cost, the **coolest** walk the heat (UTCI) cost; see [Methods](methods.qmd). ## How much sun can a walk home avoid?

Sun ↓ = sun reduction of the shadiest walk; Exposure ↓ = weighted exposure reduction. - **The shadiest walk is rarely more than a few percent longer.** Mean detours stay below 1% in every group, and 95% of shadiest walks are at most 0.7%–2.6% longer than the shortest walk, depending on the group. - **Rapid-transit walks gain more** than bus walks of the same length: stations sit in denser, taller parts of the city where a parallel street in building shade is usually available. - **Short walks have no choice.** Under 300 m, more than four in five walks have no cooler option. - **Weighted exposure falls much less than sun.** With θ near 0.2, a metre moved from sun into shade lowers the cost by only 0.2 m; the remaining heat burden of shaded walking is still counted. ::: {#eef0fe27 .cell execution_count=6} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ![Sun reduction by hour, walks of 300–800 m (dynamic θ).](results_files/figure-html/cell-7-output-1.png){width=768} ::: ::: Morning and evening, when shadows are long, offer the most; around 13:00–14:00 the sun is high and little shade is left to choose. ## Where can walkers find shade? Walks home from frequent bus stops are summarised on a 500 m grid by where people live, and the cells are grouped into three types by how sunny their 300–800 m walks are and how much of that sun can be avoided. Cells vary gradually, so the types are a convenient summary rather than sharp classes. ::: {#4867e807 .cell execution_count=8} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown execution_count=8} | Cluster | Cells | Sun on shortest | Sun reduction | No cooler option | Building height (m) | Canopy | Sidewalk km/km² | |:-------------------------|--------:|:------------------|:----------------|:-------------------|----------------------:|:---------|------------------:| | Sunny, no cooler option | 51 | 65% | 25.3% | 23% | 9.1 | 7% | 44 | | Sunny but avoidable | 322 | 80% | 1.6% | 86% | 7.6 | 9% | 31 | | Cooler, few alternatives | 137 | 74% | 9.1% | 47% | 7.9 | 9% | 34 | ::: ::: Across cells, **sidewalk density** is the strongest correlate of being able to avoid the sun (Spearman ρ = 0.42 with sun reduction), while **building height** mostly sets how sunny the walk is to begin with (ρ = −0.47 with sun share). Leafy areas start cooler but, with sparser streets, rarely offer an alternative. Explore the cells on the [city map](app/map.html). ## Rapid-transit stations Stations ranked by sun reduction for walks of 300–800 m, the six largest and four smallest. Orange solid = used only by shortest walks, cyan dashed = only by shadiest walks.](results_files/figure-html/cell-14-output-1.jpeg){} ::: ::: ## From sun to heat Shade is yes or no; heat is a temperature. The SOLWEIG model gives the UTCI, the temperature the weather feels like to the body, at every sidewalk point for the same 24 hours. On June 24 at 15:00 a typical sunlit sidewalk felt like 45.9 °C, at the edge of *extreme* heat stress (46 °C); one step into shade took off about 5 °C.

Bands: UTCI heat-stress categories.](results_files/figure-html/cell-16-output-1.png){width=768} ::: ::: - **Tree shade is as cool as building shade.** The shade cost of Wen et al. counts a metre of tree shade as half as good as building shade. In the heat model, tree shade at 15:00 takes off 112%–115% of the step from sun to building shade, slightly more than building shade itself (94% at 8:00): in the afternoon, walls and pavement that stood in the sun all day still radiate heat into shaded streets, while a tree also shades the ground under it. - **Shade does not make a walk comfortable.** Even building shade stays at *very strong* heat stress (above 38 °C) from 10:00 to 17:00 on June 24. Choosing the shaded side lowers the strain; it does not remove it. ### The coolest walk home Routing on the UTCI instead of the shade classes gives the **coolest walk**. ::: ::: {#5e5d9c0c .cell .column-page-inset-right execution_count=18} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown execution_count=18} | Mode | Walk | UTCI, shortest | Extreme heat, shortest | Shadiest: UTCI / detour | Coolest: UTCI / detour | Extreme heat ↓ shadiest / coolest | Coolest = shadiest | |:-------|:-----------|:-----------------|:-------------------------|:--------------------------|:-------------------------|:------------------------------------|:---------------------| | Bus | <300 m | 44.2 °C | 33 m | −0.18 °C / +0.14% | −0.25 °C / +0.31% | 6% / 12% | 93% | | Bus | 300⁠–⁠800 m | 44.1 °C | 100 m | −0.40 °C / +0.37% | −0.54 °C / +0.70% | 16% / 28% | 77% | | Bus | 800⁠–⁠1200 m | 44.1 °C | 195 m | −0.40 °C / +0.42% | −0.59 °C / +0.92% | 16% / 36% | 60% | | Rapid | <300 m | 43.6 °C | 38 m | −0.22 °C / +0.20% | −0.29 °C / +0.38% | 9% / 13% | 92% | | Rapid | 300⁠–⁠800 m | 43.8 °C | 104 m | −0.58 °C / +0.48% | −0.72 °C / +0.79% | 22% / 32% | 71% | | Rapid | 800⁠–⁠1200 m | 43.8 °C | 187 m | −0.65 °C / +0.45% | −0.79 °C / +0.87% | 22% / 32% | 55% | ::: ::: Walk counts as in the sun table above. UTCI = mean UTCI along the walk, change against the shortest walk. Extreme heat = metres with UTCI ≥ 46 °C on the shortest walk, and the mean reduction for walks that have any. - **The two walks mostly agree.** For 71%–77% of walks of 300–800 m the coolest walk is the shadiest walk. Where they differ, the coolest walk takes the tree-lined street the shade cost undervalues, and tells apart sunny streets that are hotter or cooler than usual. - **The coolest walk is a little cooler, for a little more distance.** It lowers the walk's mean UTCI by about 0.1 °C more than the shadiest walk and cuts the metres of extreme heat stress 1.4–2.2 times as much, for mean detours of 0.3%–0.9%. - **Rapid-transit walks gain most**, as with sun: −0.72 °C for walks of 300–800 m, against −0.54 °C from bus stops. - **Averages are small because most walks have no choice.** The mean over all walks, sunny or not, hides walks with no alternative (a change of 0) next to walks that cool by several degrees. Like shade, the gain is largest in the morning (−0.82 °C at 09:00 on June 24, all walks) and small around midday (−0.33 °C at 14:00), when little shade is left. Unlike shade, it is small again in the evening (−0.13 °C at 19:00): the shadows are long, but the low sun no longer makes the sunny side much hotter. ### Why the coolest walk is cooler ::: {#f3ce36e7 .cell execution_count=20} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=20} ![Same detour, cooler walk: mean detour and mean UTCI reduction of walks of at least 300 m at 15:00 (both days), for three costs with θ fixed from 0.05 to 0.6.](results_files/figure-html/cell-21-output-1.png){width=720} ::: ::: Is the coolest walk cooler only because it is allowed to detour more? Fixing θ at a range of values traces, for each cost, how much cooler walks get for a given extra distance. At the same detour the UTCI cost cools walks 12%–14% more than the shade cost. Valuing tree shade as much as building shade adds only about 1%: most of the gain comes from the differences *within* each shade class, such as a sunny metre next to hot walls against one on an open lawn, or a deep street canyon against a thin strip of shade. **How robust is this?** SOLWEIG lets a fixed 3% of the sun through tree crowns. Rerunning 40 tiles of June 24 with 5% and 15% moves tree shade's share of the building-shade relief at 15:00 from 112% to 110% and 99%: thinner crowns make tree shade warmer, but it stays about as cool as building shade, far from the half assumed by the shade cost. Widening the margin around each tile from 400 to 800 m, so that towers further away can cast shadows in, changes the UTCI by more than 0.5 °C at no more than 0.02% of points in any hour. Details: [technical notes](technical.qmd). ## Through buildings (University City) ::: {#51c9ce5b .cell .column-page-inset-right execution_count=23} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown execution_count=23} | Sample | Scenario | Walks | Shadiest uses indoors | Sun ↓* | Exposure ↓* | Length* | |:---------|:-----------------------------------|--------:|:------------------------|:---------|:--------------|:----------| | Campus | Outdoor only | 3,000 | 0% | 10.6% | 1.3% | +0.71% | | Campus | + buildings open without a Penn ID | 3,000 | 6% | 11.6% | 1.8% | +0.46% | | Campus | + all mapped buildings | 3,000 | 23% | 12.5% | 2.3% | +0.52% | | Station | Outdoor only | 5,204 | 0% | 15.9% | 1.7% | +1.00% | | Station | + buildings open without a Penn ID | 5,204 | 4% | 16.6% | 2.0% | +0.89% | | Station | + all mapped buildings | 5,204 | 21% | 18.2% | 2.7% | +0.73% | ::: ::: Campus = building to building; Station = rapid-transit station to building. \* compared with the shortest walk on the outdoor-only network. Indoor passages have no UTCI, so this section uses the shade cost only. Opening the annotated buildings puts about one in five shadiest walks indoors and removes another 1.9–2.3 points of sun, without making walks longer. The Indoor Contribution Index stays close to zero (median below 0.001 in absolute value): indoor passages here offer an equally long but cooler option, not a shortcut. This differs from the Dubai stations of Wen et al. (2025), where indoor networks through malls and connected towers make indoor routes real shortcuts. With θ near 0.2–0.3 for most of a 300–1,200 m walk, an indoor metre beats building shade by only about 0.1 m of cost, so indoor routes are chosen mainly when they are already on the way; walks of 800–1,200 m use them 2.4–3.0 times as often as walks of 300–800 m. ::: {#1e9c1801 .cell execution_count=25} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=25} ![University City at 15:00: share of the sun avoided compared with the shortest outdoor walk, and share of shadiest walks that go indoors.](results_files/figure-html/cell-26-output-1.png){width=691} ::: ::: ## Limitations - Outside University City, campus and park walkways are missing, so cooler options there are understated. - “No cooler option” mixes two cases: no cooler street exists, or one exists but is not worth the detour at the default shade preference. - Shadows and heat are for two hot, sunny days, June 24 and July 29, 2025; trees from leaf-off LiDAR and 2018 land cover; buildings from 2022. - Air temperature, humidity and wind come from one ERA5 weather cell and are the same on every street; the heat map shows the effect of sun, shade and surfaces, not neighbourhood differences in air temperature or the cooling of a breezy street. - Trees let a fixed 3% of the sun through in SOLWEIG; leafier or sparser crowns would change how much cooler tree shade is (see the sensitivity test above). - UTCI is for a standing person in the open air; air-conditioned indoor passages have no UTCI, so the coolest walk stays outdoors. - Indoor passages assume buildings are open and air-conditioned; opening hours and security are not modelled.
